title: Horizontal Compression of a Shifted Square Root Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Give an equation for the graph of y = sqrt(x + 1) after it is compressed horizontally by a factor of 4.

steps.title: Recall the Horizontal Compression Rule
steps.explanation: Compressing the graph of y = f(x) horizontally by a factor of c > 1 replaces x with c*x.
steps.why: Each x-coordinate is divided by c when x is replaced by c*x.

steps.title: Replace x with 4x
steps.explanation: Substituting 4x in place of x in y = sqrt(x + 1) yields y = sqrt(4x + 1).
steps.why: Note that only the variable x is multiplied by 4, not the +1 constant.

steps.title: Verify the Effect on the Domain Endpoint
steps.explanation: The original endpoint (-1, 0) moves 4 times closer to the y-axis to (-1/4, 0), while the y-intercept (0, 1) remains fixed on the y-axis.
steps.why: Horizontal compression toward the y-axis divides every x-coordinate by 4.
